Deadlock Detection

1. How Deadlocks Happen
  • A deadlock occurs when two or more transactions are waiting for each other to release locks: 
    Transaction A: locks key 1, then tries to lock key 2 (blocked by B)
Transaction B: locks key 2, then tries to lock key 1 (blocked by A)
→ Both wait forever
  • Deadlocks are possible with PESSIMISTIC transactions that access keys in different orders;
2. Deadlock Detection in Ignite
  • Ignite can detect deadlocks and report which transactions and keys are involved;
  • Enable by setting a transaction timeout — when the timeout expires, Ignite runs deadlock detection: 
    try (Transaction tx = ignite.transactions().txStart(
        PESSIMISTIC, REPEATABLE_READ, 5000, 0)) {

    cache.put(key1, val1);
    cache.put(key2, val2);
    tx.commit();
} catch (CacheException e) {
    if (e.getCause() instanceof TransactionTimeoutException) {
        System.out.println("Possible deadlock: " + e.getMessage());
    }
}
3. Preventing Deadlocks
  • Access keys in a consistent order — if all transactions lock keys in the same order (e.g., by ascending key), deadlocks cannot occur;
  • Use OPTIMISTIC + SERIALIZABLE — optimistic transactions don't acquire locks until commit, so deadlocks are not possible (but conflicts may cause retries);
  • Set transaction timeouts — ensures that deadlocked transactions are eventually rolled back;
  • Keep transactions short — hold locks for as little time as possible;
4. Deadlock-Free Transaction Pattern
  • Sort the keys before accessing them: 
    List<Integer> keys = Arrays.asList(key1, key2, key3);
Collections.sort(keys); // consistent order

try (Transaction tx = ignite.transactions().txStart(PESSIMISTIC, REPEATABLE_READ)) {
    for (Integer key : keys) {
        cache.get(key); // acquires locks in order
    }
    // perform updates...
    tx.commit();
}
